newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most stocks flat as Beirut bourse rests.
newsitem.headline: Most stocks flat as Beirut bourse rests.

text.p: Most active shares were unchanged in quiet trade on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Tuesday and brokers said the market was taking a breather after recent busy activity.
"The market was due for rest but the trend is not reversed. It is still upward," Nicholas Sawan, head of trading at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest told Reuters.
The LIBX bank index fell 1.41 percent to 193.47 and the LISPI dropped 0.67 percent to 97.59 while the BLOM general index fell 0.03 percent to 1115.25.
Bank of Beirut fell to $5.5 from $5.6875 and Banque Audi fell to $27.75 from $28. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was flat at $21.50.
Sawan pointed out that banks mid-year results had all come in line with expectations.
Solidere A and B shares were unchanged from Monday's $13 and $13.125 respectively.
"I think Solidere is getting ready for a new move upward. It is really the most undervalued stock on the market," Sawan added.
The company's global depositary receipts traded at $17.325 on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
BSE turnover rose to 293,437 shares from 258,337 for a value of $3,902,259 against $2,996,644.
Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.2813. Pipemaker Eternit rose to $2 on a turnover of 450 shares. The share had last traded at $1.78125 on June 26.
There was no trade in the other listed industrial firms -- Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
